abstract: Salgado-Puga et al. show that exposure to broadband noise during sleep disrupts hippocampal sharp-wave ripples, alters associated neuronal activity, and impairs memory consolidation. The magnitude of neural and behavioral disruption depends on sound timing relative to ripples.

title: Haplodiploidy alone does not predict the evolution of eusociality
abstract: Suresh and Linksvayer use insect phylogeny to show that transitions to eusociality are not generally driven by haplodiploid sex determination systems but strongly associated in one specific lineage, the aculeate hymenopterans that include bees, ants and wasps.

title: Embryogenesis: Centering and decentering during cleavage
abstract: As sea urchin embryos undergo reductive cleavage, nuclear position changes progressively along the apical–basal axis. A new study shows that cell size itself shifts the balance between centering and decentering forces, driving the progressive apical displacement of nuclei.

title: Motor control: Muted motor prioritization in stuttering
abstract: Mu/beta rhythms over sensorimotor cortex reflect motor control dynamics. A new study shows that these rhythms track how the brain prioritizes hand action plans as they shift over time, and that this prioritization is weaker in people who stutter.

title: Wildlife ecology: When the fearsome become fearful
abstract: Humans recreating in wilderness areas face a risk of encountering and being harmed by fearsome large wild carnivores. Yet, the risk is exceedingly low, because, it turns out, these fearsome predators become quite fearful when encountering humans.

title: Evolution: Ancient monoamines in a neuron-less animal
abstract: A new study in placozoans — tiny marine animals that lack neurons — identifies monoamine receptors, biosynthetic machinery, cellular expression patterns, and behavioural effects. Together, these findings suggest that the monoaminergic signalling system predates the emergence of bilaterians.

title: Evolutionary ecology: Islands within islands
abstract: Deep sinkhole forests shelter rare trees from climate stress but strand them in severe isolation. A new study of a karst magnolia shows interior populations lose genetic diversity and accumulate harmful mutations, suggesting climate refuges may also become evolutionary traps.

title: Microbial metabolism: Reactivating the molecular motor of the biological methane generator
abstract: The methane-generating enzyme from methanogenic archaea must be reactivated via a dedicated system. New molecular insights demonstrate that a key component of the reactivation machinery is redox sensitive, binds the methane-forming enzyme via an ATP-dependent switch, and hydrolyses ATP once bound.

title: Ecology: Honeybee queens offload pesticides to their eggs
abstract: Honeybees are eusocial, making queen health critical for colony development. Honeybee colonies are frequently exposed to pesticides. New research shows that queens can protect themselves from pesticides by transferring these toxins to their eggs when worker-mediated social buffering is overwhelmed.

title: Avian vision: A stable view of a moving world
authors: Patrick J. Lewin, Steven J. Portugal
abstract: Two new studies provide the clearest evidence yet that eye position is actively controlled during avian flight. Pigeons dynamically balance image stabilisation, optic-flow processing and binocular vision, suggesting that gaze control is integral to navigation, obstacle avoidance and landing.
